MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 22, 2016

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Ury at 5:00 p.m., on March 22, 2016, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on March 17, 2016, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:01 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/ Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the
  Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s
  Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.

City Council Minutes  1  March 22, 2016
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:00 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

INVOCATION: Council Member Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize City Volunteers for Their 1,000 Hours of Service

  Mayor Ury presented certificates of appreciation to Pauline Hobiera, Ann Marie
  Pasquariello, Judi Showalter, Nancy Livingston, Tina Roberts, and Peggy Stalter.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Gail Reavis, M.V.: expressed her opposition to the proposed changes in the City's sign ordinance
for political signs (agenda item 11.)

Wendy Ailaire, M.V.: stated that the Casta del Sol Board Members control the community with
fear and they approved a $1.27 million pool renovation project without the consent of the
homeowners. She asked why the City building officials approved the project with safety railings
missing from the entrance to the pool.

James Littlejohn and Nicole Watson, M.V.: expressed an interest in opening a dialogue with the
City about a future Boys and Girls Club in Mission Viejo.

Kevin Frabotta, General Manager of Lake Mission Viejo Association, M.V.: read a letter from the
President of the Lake Association regarding the benefits of the Advanced Purified Water Project.

Grant Voss, M.V.: presented the City Council with the 2015 Award of Excellence from the
California Parks and Recreation Society for the City's universally accessible rehabilitation of
Pavion Park.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

City Council Minutes  2  March 22, 2016
 On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of March 8, 2016, as presented.

3.  Check Register Dated February 26, 2016 in the Amount of $317,177.96

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated March 4, 2016 in the Amount of $1,007,744.65

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January 2016

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January 2016

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January
  2016

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  March 22, 2016
 8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for January 2016

  Received and filed.

9.  Amendment to the Waste Disposal Agreement Between the County of Orange and the
  City of Mission Viejo

  Adopted Resolution No. 16-07 Approving the Revised Effective Date to an Amendment
  to the 2009 Waste Disposal Agreement with the County of Orange.

10.  Revisions to City of Mission Viejo Personnel Policies

  Adopted Resolution 16-08 Providing for the Revisions to select Personnel Policies.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

NEW BUSINESS

11.  Placement of Temporary Signs in the Public Right-of-Way at Arterial Intersections
  for 45 days prior to any Government Agency Election.

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

  Ray Kromer, M.V.: strongly urged the Council to vote no. He stated that the proposed
  change is extremely self-serving for politicians and there is no benefit to the resident
  taxpayers of the City.

  Council Member Bucknum expressed her concern with the proposal. She used a
  hypothetical example directed at Council Member Raths to demonstrate negative wording
  that could be problematic to any candidate given the lack of regulations over verbiage on
  political signs.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she will be voting no because she will not put signs
  in the intersections and she doesn’t want to pay for a removal service she is not using. She
  cited visual clutter, free speech and first amendment rights as well.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Ury, to (1) approve criteria
  for the placement of temporary signs in the public right-of-way at arterial intersections for
  45 days prior to any Government Agency Election; and (2) approve Resolution 16-09
  Adopting Criteria for the Placement of Temporary Signs in the Public Right-of-Way at

City Council Minutes  4  March 22, 2016
   Arterial Intersections for 45 days prior to any Government Agency Election and Adding
  City Council Policy 0600-06.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Bucknum and Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

12.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

13.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

14.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Mayor Ury presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

15.  Mid-Year Budget Review for FY 2015/16

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to adopt
  Resolution 16-10 Amending the FY 2015/16 Budget for Adjustments to Certain Revenue
  Sources and Operating and Capital Improvement Program Appropriations.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  March 22, 2016
 16.  Support of AB 2772 (Chang) Alcohol and Other Drug Treatment Facilities

  City Manager Wilberg presented the report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Ury, to direct the City
  Manager to send letters of support for AB 2772.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

17.  Support of SB 1415 (Bates) CEQA Exemption During Declared Droughts

  Mayor Ury presented the report.

  Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to direct the City
  Manager to send letters of support for SB 1415.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

18.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths expressed his appreciation to City staff and stated that they are doing a
fantastic job.

City Council Minutes  6  March 22, 2016
 Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs announced that there will be a town hall meeting on the topic of sober
living homes on March 29, 2016, beginning at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber. He stated that
there will be a good panel of experts who can answer residents’ questions and it is an educational
process to bring residents up to date on current laws and opportunities.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht asked Council Member Bucknum to identify a date for their next PACE
ad hoc committee meeting. She stated that the PACE program is now in Sacramento County and
they too are expressing the same concerns that she keeps raising. She read from an article on the
topic and presented it to the City Clerk for the public record. Council Member Schlicht announced
that the Court of Appeals has ruled that the trial court decision on the Orange County Fire
Authority JPA second amendment was invalid and she also submitted an article on that topic. She
stated that this City needs to be proactive and start looking at alternatives if it doesn’t pan out with
the County. Other cities are looking at ways to create their own fire authority and this City should
look at options too. Council Member Schlicht announced that she is not in favor of paying for the
CustomScoop Media Monitoring Service. She feels that it is a waste of money and benefits the
Council Members, not the public. In closing, Council member Schlicht read a quote from Edmund
Burke: “The greater the power the more dangerous the abuse.”

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum thanked Senator Bates and Assemblyman Brough for the very
successful and well-attended South County Senior Day and she said it was an honor for Mission
Viejo to host that event. She also thanked the Chief of Police Services and his staff for hosting
“Coffee with a Cop.” It was a nice opportunity for the citizens to greet the deputies and everyone
seemed to have a good time. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum congratulated the Saddleback College
Foundation on its 16th Annual Gala where they honored some star students and she said that it was
wonderful to see. She discussed her participation in upcoming events including a ride along with
Meals on Wheels and the Bunny Days event which is always very popular to the community. She
thanked Congresswoman Mimi Walters for organizing a cyber-security program on March 24 and
she noted that she and Mayor Ury will be giving opening remarks. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
further thanked Council member Sachs for organizing a town hall meeting on the issue of sober
living homes and in response to a comment made earlier in the evening, she clarified that she is
not directly involved with the Casta del Sol Homeowners Association in her job duties and rather,
the Casta del Sol Board of Directors are in charge. In closing, Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum asked
Director Lister to provide clarification on the pool area renovation at Casta del Sol.

Director Lister responded that an alternation to an existing pool does not require the same level of
accessible access. Given Casta del Sol’s application and the applicable building codes, only two
handrails were installed as allowed by law.

City Council Minutes  7  March 22, 2016
 Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury thanked the residents and owners of the Heritage Point community for inviting him to
give a briefing on the City and other matters such as transportation issues within the County. He
stated that there was a very spirited discussion and he enjoyed getting in front of the residents to
talk with them. Mayor Ury expressed his condolences on the passing of former Mission Viejo
Commissioner, Richard Wu.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:47 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting in memory of Richard Wu, to Tuesday, April 12, 2016, at 5:00
p.m.

City Council Minutes  8  March 22, 2016
